create.name: Swami Sarvapriyananda
create.bio:
Swami Sarvapriyananda is a monk of the Ramakrishna Order and, since 2017, the minister and spiritual head at the Vedanta Society of New York, a centre Swami Vivekananda started in 1894. He joined the order in India in 1994 and took full monastic vows in 2004. Before moving to New York he trained young monks at Belur Math, the order's headquarters near Kolkata, worked in its educational institutions, and served as assistant minister at the Vedanta Society of Southern California. In 2019–20 he held a fellowship at Harvard Divinity School.

He teaches Advaita Vedanta, the non-dual school of Indian philosophy, by working closely through classic texts such as the Upanishads, the Mandukya Karika, the Bhagavad Gita and the Drg Drsya Viveka, joined with guided meditation and patient answers to questions. His recorded talks, many filmed at the society's house on the Upper West Side, reach a very large audience online. He often speaks with scientists and philosophers about consciousness, has taken part in interfaith events, including at the United Nations, and teaches retreats at Omega and centres around the world. His books include Mahavakya, Fullness and Emptiness, and Moments of Awakening.

books.title: Mahavakya: The Essence of Vedanta
books.author: Swami Sarvapriyananda
books.description: Edited from his lectures, this book works through the four 'great sayings' of the Upanishads, such as 'Thou art That'. It shows how each points to the identity of the individual self with Brahman and what that means for practice.

books.title: Fullness & Emptiness: Vedanta and Buddhism
books.author: Swami Sarvapriyananda
books.description: A comparison of how Vedanta speaks of ultimate reality as fullness while Buddhism speaks of it as emptiness. He traces where the two traditions meet and where they genuinely differ.

books.title: Vedanta in Practice: Conversations
books.author: Swami Sarvapriyananda
books.description: Questions put to him by students over the years, with his replies, grouped by theme. The exchanges deal with how to live Vedanta day to day: work, relationships, doubt, meditation and spiritual discipline.

books.title: Moments of Awakening: Vedantic Stories That Stir the Soul
books.author: Swami Sarvapriyananda
books.description: A collection of the teaching stories he uses in his talks, many passed down among monks of his order. Each short tale opens onto a point of Vedantic teaching, often with gentle humour.

courses.title: Inquiry Into the Seer & the Seen: Explore the Drg Drsya Viveka Text
courses.description: A three-night residential study retreat at Omega's Rhinebeck campus on the Drg Drsya Viveka, a short Advaita text on telling the witness apart from what it observes. Sessions combine close reading of the verses with silence and reflection; Vedanta Society of New York members get a discount code.

free_resources.title: Sunday Service at the Vedanta Society of New York
free_resources.description: A one-hour talk each Sunday at 11 am, usually given by Swami Sarvapriyananda, at the society's house on West 71st Street and livestreamed on YouTube. Topics range across Vedanta, the harmony of religions and spiritual life; registration details are on the page.

free_resources.title: Ask Swami Q&A
free_resources.description: A sorted library of his Sunday question-and-answer sessions, each question linked to its video answer. Also available as a podcast, with new questions accepted by email.

free_resources.title: Lectures by Scripture
free_resources.description: The society's free archive of his lecture series arranged by text, such as the Upanishads, the Bhagavad Gita and Shankara's works. Each series is offered as a video playlist and podcast with subtitles.
